title: Demo Mode: ephemeral demo harness for feature discovery — scratchpad
body:
Context / why this idea

We get many requests from PMs/solutions teams and early customers for a low-friction way to SHOW Redwood capabilities (latency, streaming, fallback routing, model variants, embeddings) against their data without a full integration. Sales demos, partner workshops, and internal hackdays all suffer from long prep and fragile environment setup.

Idea summary (one line)

An ephemeral "Demo Mode": a short-lived, sandboxed demo harness that wires a tiny sample dataset, a constrained compute profile, and a guided UI flow so a user (engineer or PM) can run 5–10 representative interactions in under 5 minutes. No billing surprises, data isolated, optional local shadowing of customer model.

Key goals
- Remove friction for feature discovery: <5 min to a meaningful demo.
- Keep cost and risk bounded: token/cpu caps, ephemeral instances, scrubbed logs.
- Surface product value: streaming, latency metrics, fallback behaviors, embeddings similarity search.
- Make it repackagable for sales, docs, and hackathons.

Primary personas
- Solutions engineer running a quick customer proof-of-concept
- Product manager evaluating latency/qualitative output for model choices
- Developer exploring SDK basics without creating keys or commit to infra

Flows & UX (sketch)
1) Entry: "Try Demo Mode" from Console or SDK quickstart page. Short form: project name, choose demo kit (conversational assistant, embeddings search, summarizer), optional upload (CSV/text) OR use sample dataset.
2) Provision: backend spins ephemeral environment (container/pool) with preconfigured model variants, tiny KV cache, and a demo control panel. Demo expires in 30 minutes.
3) Guided script: 3–5 suggested interactions with editable prompts. Each step shows cost estimate, expected latency, and a switch to toggle fallback to cheaper model for comparison.
4) Observability lite: per-request latency, token counts, and a single-line explanation if a fallback or retry occurred.
5) Export: save a short JSON manifest for later replay or handoff to engineering; optionally open a sandbox repo with the same calls.

Non-technical constraints / safety
- No real customer secrets accepted in demo upload. If user uploads sample data, it must be explicitly marked demo and will be auto-scrubbed and TTL'd.
- Limit total tokens per session (e.g., 50k tokens) and throttle streaming if needed.
- Demo runs in isolated tenancy with disabled external network calls.

User stories (rough)
- As a solutions engineer, I want to run a 3-interaction conversation with a canned support ticket dataset so I can show a customer how the model summarizes and suggests responses.
- As a PM, I want to toggle quantization/variant A/B to show latency/cost trade-offs in real time.
- As a developer, I want to click "copy SDK snippet" that reproduces the demo calls so I can embed them in a quickstart repo.

Success metrics (initial)
- Time-to-first-meaningful-interaction <= 5 minutes (measured from click-to-first-response)
- Demo conversion: % of demos that convert to follow-up (signup, sales call) within 14 days
- Average cost per demo (target < $0.75)
- % demos using uploaded sample data vs canned datasets (we want both, track safety incidents)

Acceptance criteria / MVP checklist
- Console button to start Demo Mode + tiny provisioning path (ephemeral infra)
- Three demo kits: assistant, embedding-search, summarizer with curated prompts and datasets
- UI controls: model variant toggle, token cap slider, export snippet button
- Lightweight telemetry: per-demo token usage, latency histogram, fallback counts
- Auto-expire + auto-delete demo data after TTL

Implementation sketch (backend)
- Provisioning orchestrator creates a namespaced demo session record and allocates either a local sandbox worker or tags a lightweight shared pool slot.
- Use a "demo profile" model config: small context length, lower max tokens, specific kernel selection for low-cost execution.
- Attach a short-lived API key scoped to demo session.
- Emit minimal traces to Console with demo tag and scrubbed payloads.

Quick API snippet (for export)
- SDK example should be single-file, copy-paste runnable, uses demo key and sample dataset fetch.
- Include "replay_demo(session_id)" helper to re-run interactions with the same prompts.

Risks / open questions
- Security: how to prevent upload of PII or secrets in demo uploads? (UI warning + auto-scrub but might not be enough)
- Cost: need strict caps; what happens if user tries to parallelize many demos? (rate-limit by account)
- Sales handoff: how to transition from ephemeral demo to customer's dedicated environment with minimal friction? (export manifest + onboarding playbook)

Parking lot (nice-to-have features)
- Pre-recorded "guided tour" mode with narrated steps and auto-play prompts.
- Slack/Teams share card that embeds the demo link and a 30s gif of the interaction.
- Local shadow runner: option to run demo calls against locally hosted open model for offline events.

Next steps / TODOs (short-term)
- [ ] Sync with infra SRE to validate an ephemeral worker pattern and cost model (ask: safe per-demo budget)
- [ ] Prototype console UX: one-screen flow, minimal fields
- [ ] Build 3 demo kits with curated prompts & sample datasets (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft safety policy for uploaded data with legal review (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Wire export snippet and sample quickstart repo (owner: DevEx)

Notes / stray thoughts
- Could be a huge boon for hiring/evangelism: new hires can run Demo Mode to get hands-on with product in minutes.
- Potential to bundle as a "sales playground" license for enterprise buyers (longer TTL, more capacity).
- Keep UX simple: biggest win is speed — fewer checkboxes on first pass.

End of page.
